# Storyliner

> A free tool for writing the foundational story of your brand in 160 characters — the SEO meta description most people skip. Built on 2,500 years of logic from Aristotle: ethos, pathos, logos, and a hook–tension–payoff arc. Live keyword tracking and free suggestions help you weave in the words people actually search. By Carey Balboa, IT Help San Diego Inc.

## What it is

- [The Workshop](https://seo-keyword-storyteller.replit.app/#workshop) — a 160-character editor framed by 8 keyword slots. Write your brand story; matched keywords light up live as you weave them in.
- Story Coach — a free, rule-based coach that scores your story on ethos (character/trust), pathos (feeling), and logos (logic/proof), and checks the arc: hook, tension, payoff. Always works offline; no account, no payment.
- Keyword suggestions — free, from the Datamuse API. Click a chip to drop a word into an open discovery slot (never the two hand-typed anchor slots).
- Optional AI rewrite — off by default. Point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Gemini free tier, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio) for an AI-written 160-character rewrite.

## The method

- The brand story is the FOUNDATION — it comes before the logo, the domain, the ads.
- Aristotle, compressed: ethos = the reason you can be trusted; pathos = the reason a stranger cares; logos = the concrete proof. Plus a story shape — a hook, a turn, a payoff — even in one breath.
- Keywords are honest findability, NOT a market bet. Be publicly who you say you are — name, address, and offering all matching — and the right people simply find you.
- The reality check: a keyword must name what is TRUE, even when it is not what you wish you were known for. If it is how the world finds you, it earns a slot.
- The anchor (slots #1 and #2): the first two of the eight slots are special and hand-typed. Slot #1 is "what you are" — your core category plus place (e.g. "IT support, San Diego"). Slot #2 is "who you are" — your brand name. The remaining six are the discovery words strangers actually type, and six is really all anyone needs.

## Principles for choosing keywords

- Everything matches — pick the one real-world name people call you and spell it identically everywhere (name, logo, colors, photos, descriptions). You don't put "LLC" on everything (Google even discourages legal suffixes in your Business Profile); just keep your exact registered legal name where it's official — footer, contracts, registrations — so directories match you to the real record and you read like a bigger, real brand.
- The 2 a.m. test — picture a stranger typing to solve the exact problem you fix; their words are your keywords.
- Bread & butter — every keyword should point at money; if it does not lead toward a customer, cut it.
- Name what's real — the thing you're known for is how you're found, like it or not; keywords can be short phrases too.
- Don't pay anyone to cheat — shady PR firms, SEO "growth" shops, and AI slop shops fake reviews and backlinks; search engines catch it and the penalty darkens your real brand. There is no shortcut around being who you say you are.
